title: Chiral Phonons and Giant Anisotropic Photoresponse in Quasi-1D van der Waals Semiconductor ZrSnS3
authors: Zahir Muhammad, Shashi B. Mishra, Gayatri, Grzegorz Krasucki, Wajid Ali, Katarzyna Olkowska-Pucko, Obaid Iqbal, Zia Ur Rehman, Aziz Ur Rahman, Maciej R. Molas, Lin Xiaoyang, Weisheng Zhao
abstract: Low-dimensional van der Waals semiconductors with reduced symmetry provide a unique platform for exploring anisotropic physical properties. The quasi-one-dimensional family MXQ$_3$ (M = Hf, Zr; X = Sn; Q = S, Se) exhibits notable structural anisotropy, where zigzag atomic chains influence optical phenomena such as birefringence. This study investigates anisotropic lattice dynamics in ZrSnS$_3$ using angle- and polarization-dependent Raman spectroscopy. Temperature-dependent measurements reveal anharmonic phonon behavior, indicating strong phonon-phonon coupling. Density functional theory calculations show good agreement with the experimentally observed Raman spectra, validating the microscopic description of the lattice dynamics. We also observe a helicity-dependent intensity and a reversal in phonon intensity between lower- and higher-frequency modes under circularly polarized light, which is characteristic of chiral phonons governed by the polarization of the Zr/Sn chains. Our first-principles analysis further shows that angular-momentum-like phonon textures can emerge away from the $Γ$-point near mode-hybridization and avoided-crossing regions, providing microscopic insight into the observed helicity-dependent Raman signatures. Furthermore, we fabricate an optoelectronic device from a thin ZrSnS$_3$ nanowire, demonstrating a photoresponsivity of 50~mA/W under 520~nm laser excitation (1~mW/cm$^2$). The device exhibits a pronounced, power-scalable anisotropic photoresponse with a clear preferred polarization direction. These results highlight the coupling mechanisms between polarization, lattice vibrations, and charge carriers in ZrSnS$_3$, establishing it as a promising material for polarization-sensitive optoelectronics and directional quantum transport.
summary: This work characterizes the anisotropic lattice dynamics of the 1D van der Waals semiconductor ZrSnS3 using advanced Raman spectroscopy and DFT. The study confirms strong structural anisotropy and reveals helicity-dependent phonon signatures, which are further validated by measuring a highly anisotropic photoresponse in fabricated nanowire devices. This establishes ZrSnS3 as a promising material for polarization-sensitive optoelectronics.
main_problem: The study investigates the anisotropic lattice dynamics and photoresponse in the quasi-1D van der Waals semiconductor ZrSnS3.
main_result: The material exhibits strong structural and lattice anisotropy, evidenced by helicity-dependent phonon responses and a pronounced, power-scalable anisotropic photoresponse in fabricated nanowires.
method: The research combines experimental techniques like angle- and polarization-dependent Raman spectroscopy with first-principles Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations.
model_or_system: The physical system is the quasi-one-dimensional van der Waals semiconductor ZrSnS3, belonging to the MXQ3 family, which possesses an orthorhombic structure.
key_observables: Raman spectra (unpolarized, polarized, helicity-resolved), phonon dispersion, photoresponsivity (mA/W), and temperature-dependent shifts/linewidths.
important_parameters: Temperature (e.g., 5 K), excitation wavelengths (405 nm vs. 785 nm), and polarization/helicity states.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the backscattering arrangement limits observation to certain symmetry modes, and that the Klemens model can describe anharmonic effects.
figures_summary: Figures show XRD/STEM confirmation of structure, phonon dispersion/DOS, comparison of experimental/theoretical Raman spectra, and polarization/temperature dependence maps.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by characterizing the structure (XRD/STEM), validating lattice dynamics via DFT/Raman comparison, detailing temperature and polarization dependencies (including chirality), and concluding with optoelectronic device measurements.
why_interesting: The strong coupling observed between polarization, lattice vibrations (phonons), and charge carriers in a low-dimensional material like ZrSnS3 provides a platform for understanding directional quantum transport phenomena.
